newsitem.title: EGYPT: State to sell Egyptian construction firm. [corrected 12:07 gmt]
newsitem.headline: State to sell Egyptian construction firm. [corrected 12:07 gmt]

text.p: The Egyptian state's Holding Company for Housing, Cinema and Tourism said on Tuesday it was offering the private sector 51 percent of the shares in Development and Popular Houses Company in a partial privatisation which would end state control of the company.

It has allocated 525,000 shares, or 15 percent of the total 3.5 million shares, to individuals and 910,000 shares, or 26 percent, to investment firms and mutual funds. These allocations may be increased to meet demand, the holding company said.
It is also offering 10 percent, or 350,000 shares in the construction firm, to company employees.
The offer will be open for two days only -- September 1 and 2 -- and the price will be a fixed 29 pounds a share.
The holding company said shareholders would be eligible for a dividend of at least 2.73 pounds a share for the 1995/96 fiscal year, which ended on June 30.
The company increased net profits in 1995/96 by 3.6 percent to 12 million pounds from 11.59 million in the previous year.
Sales declined 7.4 percent to 52.541 million from 56.723 million pounds in 1994/95. (Corrects by reversing figures)
